name: feynman
description: The open source AI research agent.
readmeExcerpt:
The open source AI research agent.

## Install macOS / Linux: ```bash curl -fsSL https://feynman.is/install | bash ``` Windows (PowerShell): ```powershell irm https://feynman.is/install.ps1 | iex ``` Or with npm and Node.js 22.22 or newer: `npm install -g @companion-ai/feynman`. Then sign in to a model provider: ```bash feynman setup ``` The [installation guide](https://feynman.is/docs/getting-started/installation) covers pinned versions, uninstalling, and the skills-only bundle for Codex and OpenCode. The [setup guide](https://feynman.is/docs/getting-started/setup) covers local models and editors such as Zed. ## Use ```bash feynman "what do we know about scaling laws" feynman lit "RLHF alternatives" feynman deepresearch "mechanistic interpretability" ``` | Workflow | What it does | | --- | --- | | `/deepresearch ` | Planned investigation with parallel researchers and citation checks | | `/lit ` | Literature review: consensus, disagreements, open questions | | `/review ` | Critique with severity levels and a revision plan | | `/audit ` | Paper claims compared with its public code | | `/replicate ` | Replication plan; runs only after you choose an environment | | `/recipe ` | Ranked ML training recipes with datasets and code | | `/compare ` | Source comparison matrix | | `/draft ` | Paper-style draft from research findings | | `/autoresearch ` | Bounded experiment loop against a benchmark | | `/summarize ` | Summary of a paper, repository, or PDF | Results are saved to `outputs/` (drafts to `papers/`). `/lit`, `/deepresearch`, and `/recipe` also write a provenance file listing the sources used and what was verified. ## Sources Feynman searches alphaXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, arXiv, PubMed, Europe PMC, bioRxiv, medRxiv, Crossref, the web, and Hugging Face, and reads local PDFs and documents. Free `OPENALEX_API_KEY` and `SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY` keys avoid the shared rate limits. It runs on stock [Pi](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi) with four research agents: researcher, verifier, reviewer, and writer. ## Telemetry Feynman sends anonymous usage data to PostHog: commands, workflows, tools, models, token counts, and errors with their messages and stack traces (your home folder shown as `~`). It never sends prompts, model output, paper content, or tool arguments. Turn it off with `FEYNMAN_TELEMETRY=off`. [What is sent](https://feynman.is/docs/getting-started/configuration#telemetry) ## Contributing ```bash git clone https://github.com/Companion-Inc/feynman.git cd feynman npm install npm test ``` See [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md). [Docs](https://feynman.is/docs) · [Release notes](RELEASES.md) · [MIT License](LICENSE)
readmeHtml:
The open source AI research agent.

Install

macOS / Linux:

curl -fsSL https://feynman.is/install | bash

Windows (PowerShell):

irm https://feynman.is/install.ps1 | iex

Or with npm and Node.js 22.22 or newer: npm install -g @companion-ai/feynman.

Then sign in to a model provider:

feynman setup

The installation guide covers pinned versions, uninstalling, and the skills-only bundle for Codex and OpenCode. The setup guide covers local models and editors such as Zed.

Use

feynman "what do we know about scaling laws"
feynman lit "RLHF alternatives"
feynman deepresearch "mechanistic interpretability"
Workflow What it does
/deepresearch <topic> Planned investigation with parallel researchers and citation checks
/lit <topic or lab> Literature review: consensus, disagreements, open questions
/review <paper or draft> Critique with severity levels and a revision plan
/audit <paper> Paper claims compared with its public code
/replicate <paper> Replication plan; runs only after you choose an environment
/recipe <task> Ranked ML training recipes with datasets and code
/compare <topic> Source comparison matrix
/draft <topic> Paper-style draft from research findings
/autoresearch <idea> Bounded experiment loop against a benchmark
/summarize <source> Summary of a paper, repository, or PDF

Results are saved to outputs/ (drafts to papers/). /lit, /deepresearch, and /recipe also write a provenance file listing the sources used and what was verified.

Sources

Feynman searches alphaXiv, Semantic Scholar, OpenAlex, arXiv, PubMed, Europe PMC, bioRxiv, medRxiv, Crossref, the web, and Hugging Face, and reads local PDFs and documents. Free OPENALEX_API_KEY and SEMANTIC_SCHOLAR_API_KEY keys avoid the shared rate limits. It runs on stock Pi with four research agents: researcher, verifier, reviewer, and writer.

Telemetry

Feynman sends anonymous usage data to PostHog: commands, workflows, tools, models, token counts, and errors with their messages and stack traces (your home folder shown as ~). It never sends prompts, model output, paper content, or tool arguments. Turn it off with FEYNMAN_TELEMETRY=off. What is sent

Contributing

git clone https://github.com/Companion-Inc/feynman.git
cd feynman
npm install
npm test

See CONTRIBUTING.md.

releases.name: v0.5.58
releases.body:
## v0.5.58 - 2026-10-26

- **pi-subagents 0.83.0.**
  - Background research subagents that finished their work always report it, instead of ending as "exited with code 0 before writing a result"; a foreground subagent whose child stops after its final reply returns instead of hanging.
  - Turns after a subagent returns keep the prompt cache on models that take mid-conversation system messages, so they are cheaper and faster.
  - pi-subagents now uses a patched `undici` (8.12.3), so only Pi's own pinned copy remains (see v0.5.57).
- **pi-web-access 0.45.0.**
  - The web tools add about 1.1k tokens to every model request instead of 2.8k.
  - DuckDuckGo search no longer gets your IP blocked by its bot check when several searches run at once.
  - `source_check` shows the matching passages under each source.
  - `feynman search set ninerouter <base-url>` selects a self-hosted [9router](https://github.com/decolua/9router) gateway.

releases.name: v0.5.57
releases.body:
## v0.5.57 - 2026-10-24

- **Security updates from advisories published Oct 23.**
  - `undici` 8.12.3, now a direct dependency, so a fresh install no longer gives every package the pinned 8.10.2 below ([GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xjj6-f33q-929c), [GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-4qv8-2p9j-2685), [GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-f72v-6w45-q472)).
  - `body-parser` 2.4.0, `fast-uri` 3.1.9 and `zod` 4.6.7, through Alpha Hub's MCP SDK.
  - The website's build tools (vite 8.3.5, sharp 0.35.5, hono 4.13.13 and others) are patched too; its full `npm audit` is clean.
- Pi 1.4.0 and pi-subagents 0.81.0 still pin `undici` 8.10.2 for their own HTTP clients. Feynman can't change those copies; they'll move when Pi ([pi#11208](https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/11208)) and pi-subagents ([#3022](https://github.com/nicobailon/pi-subagents/issues/3022)) release patched versions.

releases.name: v0.5.56
releases.body:
## v0.5.56 - 2026-10-23

- **pi-subagents 0.81.0.**
  - A research subagent asked for structured output that forgets to return it gets one more turn to do so, instead of failing and losing its work.
  - The main session can tell subagent completion notices apart from text you typed.
  - In fullscreen, you can click a subagent in the inspector to select it and scroll its output with the mouse or trackpad.
  - Windows: Feynman starts faster, and no longer freezes for about 8 seconds at startup when the subagent temp folder has broken permissions.

releases.name: v0.5.55
releases.body:
## v0.5.55 - 2026-10-22

- **Clearer hints for two more OpenAI errors.**
  - A project without access to a model (`403 ... does not have access to model`) now says the account can't use that model, instead of saying your credentials were rejected.
  - "Request too large ... tokens per min" now says the request is bigger than the account's per-minute token limit, so retrying won't help.

releases.name: v0.5.54
releases.body:
## v0.5.54 - 2026-10-22

- **Two more model errors explain themselves.** When a run ends on an error, Feynman names the cause:
  - A `404 Not Found` from the provider says the model id or endpoint doesn't exist, and to check the model with `/model` and the `baseUrl` in `models.json`.
  - "The model refused to complete the request" says the model declined, and to rephrase or pick another model.
- `ip-address` 10.7.4 (through Alpha Hub's MCP SDK) fixes [GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-rxp7-6hxx-x8q5), a slow parse of long IPv6 zone identifiers.

aiSummary.oneLiner: Terminal-based, open-source AI agent that automates deep technical research and information synthesis.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: The Feynman CLI provides a robust, open-source command-line interface dedicated to conducting autonomous AI-driven research. By executing directly from the terminal, it accepts a research prompt and autonomously scours numerous web sources, documentation, and papers. It seamlessly compiles scattered technical data into unified, easily comprehensible research briefs and summaries. The tool is explicitly designed to offload the manual burden of reading through extensive literature, delivering synthesized findings straight to the developer's workspace. It utilizes specialized agents for researching, reviewing, drafting, and verifying information.
keyFeatures: Command-line interface: Delivers a comprehensive autonomous research experience executing entirely within the terminal.
Automated web scraping: Autonomously navigates and extracts critical data from highly relevant technical sources and databases.
Deep synthesis: Parses and rewrites complex, multi-source topics into clear, digestible, and cited educational summaries.
Open-source core: Allows researchers to fully inspect and modify the underlying agentic reasoning and execution logic.
Simple installation: Provides a highly streamlined, single-command installation script tailored for UNIX systems.
Specialized sub-agents: Deploys dedicated agents for evidence gathering, internal critique, structured drafting, and rigorous citation verification.

useCases.title: Accelerated learning
useCases.description: Using the CLI to rapidly gather and summarize the core concepts and architectural patterns of an unfamiliar technology stack.

useCases.title: Documentation gathering
useCases.description: Autonomously collecting and synthesizing scattered API endpoints and community usage examples into a single coherent document.

useCases.title: Background research
useCases.description: Running the agent in a dedicated terminal pane to compile context on a bug while actively debugging the code in another pane.

useCases.title: Terminal-centric workflows
useCases.description: Keeping all research, drafting, and development tasks completely contained within the CLI, deliberately avoiding browser distractions.

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers, students, and technical researchers seeking an open-source, terminal-native assistant to automate deep topical research. It specifically targets power users who demand rapid insights without the friction of manual web browsing.
